summary: Selects, orders, filters, and renames channels from one or more CHOPs. Use it for explicit CHOP routing across networks, control-panel channel extraction, and pattern-based channel shaping.

key_params.name: chop
key_params.note: Source CHOP or CHOP pattern to pull channels from when not using a wired input.

key_params.name: channames
key_params.note: Channel name patterns to keep; order determines output order and repeated names are included multiple times.

key_params.name: renamefrom
key_params.note: Channel pattern to rename using Pattern Matching.

key_params.name: renameto
key_params.note: Replacement pattern used to generate output channel names.

key_params.name: filterbydigits
key_params.note: Restricts selection to channels ending in the specified digits.

key_params.name: digits
key_params.note: Digits that selected channel names must end with when Filter by Digits is enabled.

key_params.name: stripdigits
key_params.note: Removes the matching trailing digits from selected channel names.

key_params.name: align
key_params.note: Handles multiple input CHOPs with different start or end intervals.

key_params.name: autoprefix
key_params.note: Prefixes duplicate channel names with source node names to avoid collisions.

key_params.name: timeslice
key_params.note: Forces output channels to be time sliced on the Common page.

key_params.name: scope
key_params.note: Restricts which channels are affected by Common-page CHOP operations.

key_params.name: srselect
key_params.note: Chooses how to handle mismatched input sample rates.

key_params.name: exportmethod
key_params.note: Chooses how selected channels connect to destination parameters for exports.

key_params.name: autoexportroot
key_params.note: Root path for Channel Name is Path:Parameter export destinations.

key_params.name: exporttable
key_params.note: DAT table storing export information for DAT Table export methods.

common_gotchas: Channel Names determine output order, and specifying the same channel multiple times outputs duplicates in that order.
Rename and extraction options apply when using the CHOP and Channel Name parameters; verify behavior separately when routing from a wired input.
Automatic Prefix is useful when duplicate channel names from multiple sources would otherwise collide.
Use Align deliberately when selected CHOPs have different start/end intervals; the choice can trim, extend, shift, or stretch channels.
